Under the DPDP Act, 2023, failing to adhere to any term of an accepted voluntary undertaking is deemed a breach of the provisions of the Act, and the Board may proceed under section 33 [1]. Under section 33, if the Board determines after an inquiry that the breach is significant, it may impose the monetary penalty specified in the Schedule, taking into account factors such as the nature, gravity, and duration of the breach [1], [3]. 

However, the provided excerpts do not contain the Schedule, so the exact monetary amount of the penalty is missing.

ed28dae9be09c6fb3e58f5efe8ddcbd917f10ff9.text:
The Central Government appoints the Chairperson after considering the suitability of individuals recommended by a Search-cum-Selection Committee [1], [3]. 

This Search-cum-Selection Committee recommends individuals for the appointment and consists of:
- The Cabinet Secretary as chairperson [3];
- The Secretaries to the Government of India in charge of the Department of Legal Affairs and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology as members [3]; and
- Two experts of repute with special knowledge or practical experience in a field deemed useful to the Board by the Central Government as members [3].

45d4e92dd05760e4d908e7d70e7d6b3cbb662ca4.text: Based on the provided excerpts, there is no mention of courts, tribunals, or whether they can process personal data without following the Act's duties. Therefore, the excerpts do not contain enough information to answer the question.

8b106dc04b3fa5c0f4b487b86a545b08f5a424b7.text:
Yes, to a significant extent. Under Section 17(1)(b) of the Act, when personal data is processed by any court or tribunal in India and such processing is necessary for the performance of any judicial or quasi-judicial function, the provisions of Chapter II (Obligations of Data Fiduciary), Chapter III, and Section 16 do not apply [2]. 

However, they are not completely exempt from all duties: sub-sections (1) and (5) of section 8 under Chapter II still apply [2]. (Note: The provided excerpts do not specify the exact text of Section 8(1) and (5) [2]).

6fc8e983ed7bef46905edfba94c66e2297dbd0e4.text:
Under Section 17(1)(d), where personal data of Data Principals not within the territory of India is processed by a person based in India pursuant to a contract entered into with a person outside India, certain provisions—specifically Chapter II (except subsections (1) and (5) of section 8), Chapter III, and section 16—do not apply [1], [3]. 

While Section 3 generally applies the Act to the processing of digital personal data within India [2], the excerpts do not provide the full text of the Act to specify every remaining obligation that applies to such an outsourcing firm.
